person.about_me:
I’ve been fortunate to enjoy more than 35 years of successful retail growth from a start-up to a globally recognized brand in Superdry. 

My first foray into fashion retail was at the age of 19, when I used a government-backed enterprise scheme to set up my own clothing business, which I was able to sell for a profit two months later. In 1985 I started Cult Clothing, my first nationwide fashion chain which quickly grew to around £20 million turnover.

Spotting a massive shift in the marketplace and the opportunities of vertical retailing, I founded Superdry in 2003, a brand that combines an appreciation for British tailoring, a love of vintage Americana and an eye for Japanese imagery.  Starting with a collection of just five t-shirts, the brand flourished, and Superdry became a British success story recognized all over the world. 

Seven years later, at a time when many others were looking to private equity for financing, I led the float of Superdry on the London Stock Exchange, which valued the company at £400m. I am proud that the business is publicly listed in the UK and I am still the largest shareholder.

After stepping down as CEO to concentrate on product design in 2015, I returned as CEO three years later to lead the charge to fulfil Superdry’s global potential, with the same energy and excitement I’ve always had for the business.

Today Superdry operates through 740 branded locations in 61 countries, including 241 owned stores across the UK, mainland Europe and the US. Supported by a strong new leadership team and with a renewed focus on product design and digital engagement with customers, the reset of the brand is well underway. 

Sustainability has always been an integral part of the growth of Superdry and we are more focused than ever on making Superdry one of the world’s most sustainable listed fashion brands. We are making good progress on this, and I am committed to driving progressive change and leaving a positive legacy for future generations.

person.headline: Chief Executive | @Shoosmiths
person.about_me:
David is Chief Executive of Shoosmiths. He is responsible for delivering the firm’s strategy and for driving operational excellence in the business to help serve Shoosmiths’ clients.
 
Prior to taking on the role in 2022, David practised as a specialist Technology & Outsourcing lawyer, leading Shoosmiths’ award-winning national Commercial Group for over ten years. He was recognised by the directories as a Leading Individual in his field, being described as ‘very pragmatic, very commercial and technically brilliant’.
 
David is passionate about client service and innovating to create new ways of solving clients’ problems. He won the prestigious Client Partner of the Year Award at the British Legal Awards and was included in the Lawyer’s Hot 100 List of 2023.  David was also shortlisted in the Innovative Leader category of the FT’s Innovative Lawyers Europe Awards in 2022.
 
As Chief Executive, David combines leadership and management of the firm’s three core divisions (Corporate, Real Estate & Advisory Services) and its support directorates and is focused on uniting Shoosmiths’ people in the pursuit of excellence for the benefit of its clients and colleagues alike.
 
David joined Shoosmiths in 2006 from an in-house counsel role. During his time with the firm, he served on its Partnership Council for six years and led the team responsible for creating connected services offering ‘Shoosmiths8’.

He co-wrote the book ‘Legal Practice in the Digital Age’ in 2023, in which he and his fellow authors explore how the legal profession can adapt and thrive in the post-pandemic era.
 
In his role as CEO, David is committed to working hard to encourage more diversity of thought, perspective and experience at Shoosmiths and he has a personal passion, based on his own life experiences, to see improved social mobility across the profession.

Founder and managing director of the AES Engineering Group of companies. Since forming AESSEAL® in 1979, the company has grown to become one of the world’s leading specialists in the design and manufacture of mechanical seals, bearing protection and seal support systems. Our solutions not only help to improve the reliability of rotating equipment but also lower emissions, reduce water use and provide an excellent return on investment.

In 2020 AESSEAL plc was verified as Net Zero Carbon Emissions thanks to our own policies and procedures, our crusade to help prevent global warming and the positive response of our customer-base.

Today we employ more than 1700 people and provide customer service from 230 locations in 104 countries. 

Betterworld Solutions

In view of the urgency of the climate crisis, we have created the Betterworld Solutions movement to encourage Boards of companies worldwide to create a simple to understand policy to encourage sustainability projects. We believe that profitability, jobs and economic growth can go hand in hand with environmentally-friendly policies.

Our Group of Companies at AES Engineering has made environmental projects a priority for many years, but recent events have convinced us that we need a direct conduit from our own operators and suppliers.  
 
We estimate that widespread adoption of more climate-friendly policies in industry globally, could have the equivalent impact of taking 529.5 million cars off the roads.

Find out more about the drive to encourage business leaders to adopt a policy supporting the fight against global warming at https://betterworld.solutions.

Colin Buckley is responsible for British International Investment’s relations with external stakeholders and oversees its legal, compliance and communications functions. He has previously held the positions of Chief Operating Officer and Head of Strategy. He joined BII in 2013.

Colin began his career in international development working for the International Finance Corporation, ultimately managing IFC’s corporate governance projects in the former Soviet Union. After the Russo-Georgian war of 2008, he advised the Prime Minister of Georgia on the country’s economic reconstruction.

Prior to his work in international development, Colin practiced as a US attorney and a UK solicitor in Boston and London. He advised clients on public offerings, private placements, private equity, debt, venture capital, securitization and other significant cross-border transactions. In 2000, he represented FICS, a Belgian company, in the first cross-border internet transaction over $1 billion.

In 2023, Colin served as General Manager of the Association of European Development Finance Institutions (EDFI). Since 2023, he has served as Special Advisor to the FCDO on the economic reconstruction of Ukraine. Colin is a member of the Council on Foreign Relations.

person.headline: Chief Executive Officer | @Fitch Learning
person.about_me:
We believe one of the most highly prized assets a person (or company) can possess is diversity in skills and knowledge. I'm proud we can partner with clients from the Americas, to Europe and across the Emerging Markets of the Middle East, Africa and Asia. Our global reach allows us to serve our clients diverse needs wherever they are and through a number of different mediums.
 
Fortunately, my career has provided me with a broad diversity of experience and adventure! 

Early on I qualified as an accountant working in both professional services and then for a international media company. I then decided to move into education and became a financial trainer, specialising in tax, valuation and investment related topics.
 
Training became my entrée into HSBC Investment Bank where I travelled extensively between London, New York, Dubai and Asia, delivering programs to the Global Markets and Private Banking divisions. I was promoted to Head of Learning and became one of the bank’s youngest ever directors.
 
Subsequently, as a Head of Leadership, Learning and Development at Barclays Wealth, my role widened to include digital learning, performance management and talent strategy. It was a time of global financial turmoil; and at one point, I was part of the team responsible for successfully integrating and on-boarding the Lehman Brothers operation.
 
In 2011 I joined 7city (acquired by Fitch Group in 2013) to start up the Middle East & Africa business, in early 2014 I also became responsible for the Asia Pacific region. Later in 2014 I agreed (and was honoured) to become CEO of Fitch Learning.
 
Fitch Learning is the global leader in financial education. We’re strong commercially and understand our clients’ drivers and the complexities of our industry. We're proud that the worlds leading Financial Institutions invite us to partner with them to develop their most valuable asset - people.

person.headline: Ceo & founder | @BOXPARK
person.about_me:
Roger Wade is a visionary entrepreneur with over 30 years of experience in consumer brands. He is the Chairman of BoxFund VC, a venture capital firm established in 2023 that invests in early-stage UK businesses aiming to make a positive social and environmental impact.  ￼

In 1989, Roger founded Boxfresh, a pioneering British streetwear brand that introduced labels like Carhartt, G-Star, and Penfield to the UK market. He expanded Boxfresh from a market stall to an international brand operating in over 12 countries. In 2005, he sold Boxfresh to Pentland Brands and subsequently established Brands Incorporated, a consultancy specializing in the development, financing, and licensing of UK fashion brands.  ￼

In 2011, Roger launched Boxpark Shoreditch, the world’s first pop-up mall constructed from repurposed shipping containers. He expanded the concept with Boxpark Croydon in 2016 and Boxpark Wembley in 2018, creating unique spaces that blend retail, dining, and entertainment. In 2021, Roger sold a majority stake in Boxpark to Lloyds Development Capital and transitioned to the role of Non-Executive Director.  ￼

Roger has completed executive programs in ESG, Private Equity, Venture Capital, and Leadership from London Business School, Imperial College Business School, and Saïd Business School at the University of Oxford between 2020 and 2024. He is a regular columnist, speaker, lecturer, and judge on topics related to retail, fashion, branding, and entrepreneurship.

Throughout his career, Roger has been committed to supporting businesses that align profitability with purpose, fostering ventures that contribute positively to society and the environment.

person.headline: Group CEO | @Stubben Edge
person.about_me:
Stubben Edge is a technology-based financial services group that enables intermediaries and their clients to make easy decisions about their risks and how to protect or save against them, putting their success at the heart of everything we do so people can get back to what really matters. 

Its two businesses include Lucid UX, which tailors software, data and analytics solutions for clients across multiple regulated sectors. For those clients Stubben Edge Risk leverages its relationships, actuarial and product knowledge to develop niche products alongside both intermediaries and financial institutions.

The Group launched in 2018 in response to the need in the financial services industry for a partner who could provide deep market understanding and the technology, data and capacity to deliver innovation at speed. 

Our view is that existing intermediaries are in the best position to disrupt and adapt and it is our job to help them – so that more people can get the financial advice they need. With many insurance providers constrained by a one-size-fits-all approach to solutions and products, Stubben Edge instead offer their clients bespoke solutions, expert knowledge, cutting-edge technology, and the ability to structure across multiple financial services markets UK-wide and internationally.

Lucid UX, as well as being the technology engine room of the group, has also delivered a range of solutions, tools and apps for clients in other regulated sectors including finance, healthcare and engineering. Lucid’s sole purpose has been to help these clients overcome and thrive in these environments through the delivery of agile, scalable solutions to meet an ever-changing landscape of technology and regulation.

For an intermediary looking to access products for the average customer on the street seeking insurance, Stubben Edge Risk have compiled a selection of niche and complementary products across all sectors that cover the gaps that big insurers either can’t or won’t service. The company’s aim is to provide cover that is suitable for all circumstances because they believe it is their duty to ensure they can minimise the impact of the lottery of life as much as possible.

I am a passionate ambassador for organisational culture and growing talent ,ensuring the business is equipped to stay ahead of the challenges presented by changes in both customer and commercial demands.

People Operations

person.headline: HR Director | @Hush
person.about_me:
I’d be far from being called an academic across my school years, but I was always interested in human behaviour and so studying business & psychology gave me the opportunity to put a little science and theory behind the day to day interactions that had triggered my interest.

After University, as many of us do, I took a year out. I wanted to travel and work in various environments to see what suited me best. Did I want to work for a big or small company? Did I want to work in the public or private sector? Experiencing them first hand was the only way to know.

One of my earliest experiences took me to Siemens, where I watched a small HR team engage on such a breadth of topics and where 9-5 was not a concept we affiliated with. After a stint supporting recruitment at Accenture, I moved to Avon Cosmetics, to what was at the time, my dream job. I “grew up” around some great leaders at Avon, working in areas of the business that encouraged me to be creative and bold. I reflect on my Avon days in the most positive of ways, but ultimately, my time had come to move on.

So after nearly 10 years, I joined a small, international, specialist negotiation company where I focussed on global people processes and worked with the most passionate group of individuals I could imagine existing in a 250-person business. Working with C-Suite Leaders on designing talent processes, thinking differently about driving and measuring engagement, understanding opportunities to improve HR efficiency across our 13 markets, opening new markets and gaining more change and OD experience day after day.

I set up a business as a Fractional CPO and work as a Coach to my HR community and peers in leadership roles. This is where I returned to my roots and got be CPO/HRD for Medik8 and most recently Sephora and their return to the UK market (finally!!) #goals. 

Some may disagree on the role luck has to play in life, but I consider myself incredibly lucky when I reflect on my career to date…

I’ve travelled extensively, have lived in the UK, Madrid and New York, and so often find myself thinking of the 13yr old version of myself who would have laughed at the idea this would be life. I’ve met some of my closest friends through work and strive to help others see the importance of loving what you do, who you do it with and of course having a few laughs along the way.
